title: Only one publication supported a shared-control ozone dose comparison for abundance in a 2024 invertebrate data release
abstract: We audited direct support for ozone dose comparisons in a public invertebrate data release. We selected 458 usable ozone rows from 75 source publications. Exact matching of publication, outcome, taxon, measurement, control and reported context gave 34 dose series from 13 publications. Only one publication supported an abundance comparison. None supported a diversity comparison. The one abundance series had a high-dose to low-dose mean ratio of 0.644 at 150 versus 50 ppb. This is a descriptive contrast from one paper, with no uncertainty estimate. Independent abundance and diversity tests across regions and publication eras were not possible under the match rules. Missing context, exact labels, study selection and source errors limit the audit. These results do not show equal dose responses or invalidate the original meta-analysis. Climate interactions were not tested. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and independent count checks are included.

display.caption: Publications with at least two elevated ozone levels under broad and strict matching rules. Counts describe the source release and do not estimate pollution effects.
